1. Build a small argparse-compatible parser module for `--a`, `-h/--help`, duplicate handling, `--a=value`, and argparse-style error/help text.

3. Wire an ESM entry file at `/output/test4.mjs`, then run the Node version against the provided executable on representative cases and adjust any mismatches.

item.text:
Generated the ESM migration under `/output`. The library files are:

- [keywords.mjs](/output/lib/keywords.mjs)
- [char-class.mjs](/output/lib/char-class.mjs)
- [cli.mjs](/output/lib/cli.mjs)
- [sql-formatter.mjs](/output/lib/sql-formatter.mjs)

The entry file is [test4.mjs](/output/test4.mjs).

I verified the Node version against `/workspace/dataset/test4_executable` on the provided samples plus CLI edge cases like `-h`, missing `--a`, `--a=value`, duplicate `--a`, negative-number values, unknown args, quoted strings/comments, function-call keywords, and same-line whitespace after `;`. Normal statement-form inputs matched the executable behavior. The main residual risk is `sqlparse`’s odd handling of some keyword-looking identifiers after `.` in pathological SQL, which is not a typical target case.
